observations.text: SP performed the ground procedures at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the sequence of the Before Start and Before Taxiing checks. Use of the A/C levers and switches was correct once each item was called, but no item was initiated from the checklist flow alone. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent initiation of the normal procedures described in the Flight Manual is expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP, applying the checklist flow prepared during the pre-flight study, executed the normal procedures with verbal prompts from the IP required only at the fuel panel, and no part of the procedure had to be directed or executed by the IP. The two mis-selections were recognized and corrected after prompting, and cooperation with the ground crew was maintained without mis-apprehensions throughout the start sequence. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the ground procedures with minor errors in the switch sequence of the Before Taxiing checks, each one recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The A/C condition was specified and its flight permissibility decided confidently at the walk-around. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, and skipped no procedure required by the LAP and the SOPs. Awareness of the ground crew's position was verified before every switch actuation and every movement of the A/C controls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, applying an accurate and standardized checklist flow, executed the normal procedures of the Flight Manual, the Local Area Procedures and the SOPs with no omission and with correct use of all A/C levers and switches. Coordination with the ground crew was explicit, and the A/C was stopped as required at the last chance area without oscillations and without IP's intervention. Accuracy and speed in the ground phase were above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized scan of the checklist columns, could not complete the Engine Start procedure without assistance, omitting the verification of the A/C levers and switches required before the start sequence. The result was that the IP had to direct and execute part of the procedure. Further study of the normal procedures described in the Flight Manual is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not specify the A/C condition and could not decide its flight permissibility after the discrepancy found at the walk-around. The IP had to direct the reference to the Flight Manual and complete the assessment. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP completed the ground procedures at the desired standard for the Training Section, with the checks accomplished after the IP's verbal prompts at the Before Taxiing and line-up items. Errors in the switch selections were recognized and corrected with delay, and no procedure of the LAP or the SOPs was skipped once prompted. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a self-initiated checklist flow is expected in the following sorties.

SP executed the ground procedures with minor errors in the sequence of the Before Taxiing checks, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's verbal prompting or intervention. The specified taxi route was followed and the ground path of the A/C was kept clear of obstacles. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, demonstrating accuracy and speed in all normal procedures. Cooperation with the ground crew was conducted without allowing mis-apprehensions, and the A/C was stopped as required without oscillations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, applying a disciplined checklist flow and explicit coordination with the ground crew, executed the normal procedures of the Flight Manual, the LAP and the SOPs with no omission and with correct use of all A/C levers and switches. Questions on the BOTH procedures were asked and the instructor's answer was awaited before any action, and no A/C movement was allowed during the leak check. Speed and accuracy in the ground phase exceeded the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect technique of reading the checklist from memory instead of item by item, did not execute the Before Taxiing checks according to the checklist, leaving three items unverified. The IP had to interrupt the sequence and execute part of the procedure. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to distraction from the primary task by an unrelated switch action, was not aware of the ground crew's position and moved the flight controls before the clear signal was received. The result was that the check was interrupted by the IP, who took over the remainder of the sequence. Awareness of the ground crew's position before any switch actuation or control movement is to be re-briefed.

SP, due to a non-standardized checklist flow, did not perform the Before Start checks in the prescribed sequence, omitting the canopy and seat items. The checks were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the omissions were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar procedure that replaced an active reference to the checklist, skipped two items of the taxi checks required by the LAP and the SOPs. The items were accomplished only after the IP's verbal prompts, with recognition and correction delayed until the holding point. No consequence to the A/C resulted, but the procedure was not completed independently.

SP performed the ground procedures within the desired standards; however, minor deviations from the specified taxi route were twice corrected without IP's intervention. Use of the A/C levers and switches was correct and no procedure of the LAP or the SOPs was skipped. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in taxi route discipline is expected to improve.

SP executed all checks according to the checklist, without IP's intervention, in an impeccable and standardized manner, and specified the A/C condition and its flight permissibility correctly and confidently. Taxi was conducted on the specified route with the ground path kept clear of obstacles, and the A/C was stopped as required without oscillations. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, having planned the mission according to A/C energy planning and his training level, executed the briefing according to the Mission Briefing Guide and accomplished every normal procedure without omission and without IP's intervention. The A/C condition was specified and its flight permissibility decided correctly and confidently, and the alternative mission was planned and briefed as well. Accuracy and speed in the ground phase were above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect technique in the use of the A/C levers and switches, did not execute the Engine Start according to the Flight Manual, selecting the wrong position on the fuel panel without detecting it. The IP had to intervene and execute part of the procedure in order to keep the start within limits. The ground procedures were not completed without assistance.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the ground crew's position during the pre-taxi phase, released the brakes before the marshaller's signal, allowing the A/C to move while it should have been halted for the leak check. The IP intervened, stopped the A/C and directed the remainder of the sequence. The procedure was not completed without assistance and is to be repeated under supervision.

SP, due to an unstructured cross-check between the checklist and the cockpit panels, did not verify the switch positions of the Before Taxiing checks in the prescribed order, leaving two items unconfirmed. The checks were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with recognition and correction delayed by one taxi segment.

SP, due to workload management that left the checklist unfinished before the taxi clearance, did not complete the taxi checks before the A/C was moved from the parking position. The remaining items were accomplished only after the IP's verbal prompts and the omission was recognized with delay at the holding point. Cooperation with the ground crew was maintained, but the sequence prescribed by the LAP and the SOPs was not respected.

SP, due to a late power reduction during taxi, stopped the A/C at the last chance area with two slight oscillations before the final stop. The deviation was minor and was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. All remaining checks were executed according to the checklist.

SP, due to failure to pass the required call to the ground crew at the briefed point, allowed a short mis-apprehension over the chocks removal signal during the start sequence. The misunderstanding was identified and clarified by SP in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the sequence continued according to the SOPs. The error was minor and did not affect the assessment of the A/C condition or its flight permissibility.

SP executed the ground procedures within the desired standards, accomplishing all checks according to the checklist without IP's intervention. The Before Start flow was slower than the standard for this unit and two items were re-checked before the A/C condition and its flight permissibility were confirmed. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed in the execution of the normal procedures is expected to improve while the present accuracy is maintained.

SP executed every check according to the checklist, without IP's intervention and without omitting any procedure of the LAP or the SOPs, using all A/C levers and switches correctly and confidently. The specified taxi route was followed with the ground path continuously verified clear of obstacles, and the A/C was stopped as required without oscillations. Questions on the BOTH procedures were asked and the instructor's answer was awaited before any action. Above end of block MIF achieved.
